leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Define a custom hook function with TypeScript generics to encapsulate keyboard event logic.
Implement the useState hook to manage and update the pressed state of a specific key.
Apply the useEffect hook to set up and clean up event listeners for keyboard events.
Use the useCallback hook to memoize event handler functions for performance optimization.
Execute conditional logic to compare event keys with the target key and update state accordingly.
Construct event listener functions that handle both keydown and keyup events.
Utilize TypeScript interfaces to define proper types for keyboard event parameters.
Return boolean state values from the custom hook to indicate key press status.
Invoke the custom useKeyPress hook within functional components to access keyboard state.
Control component behavior by applying the returned key press state in conditional rendering.
Modify event handler logic to handle case-insensitive key comparisons when needed.
Access the custom hook's return value to trigger side effects or state updates in components.
